_bijection_arbitrary_comment: VAs whose NAME was assigned by a bijection over a reloc-masked BYTE-IDENTICAL equivalence class (laneAK). objdiff pairs by name then compares bytes, so ANY bijection within such a class scores 100% on every pair -- the MATCH is true and byte-verified, but WHICH name belongs on WHICH VA is NOT established. Same doctrine as _icf_arbitrary, at larger scale. Any tool deriving identity, callers, or unit ownership from these entries must treat them as UNRESOLVED. ***CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (lane RULER-SWEEP) -- THE CLAUSE THAT STOOD HERE IS NOW FALSE.*** It read: 'an oracle may refine the assignment later WITHOUT CHANGING ANY SCORE'. That was true only of the functionRelocDiffs=none ruler and is FALSE since name_check shipped 2026-08-12 (d04c83df). objdiff now compares a relocation's TARGET NAME (objdiff-core diff/code.rs, reloc_match under FunctionRelocDiffs::NameCheck), so every name in this list is CHARGED at every call site referencing it: the right name costs nothing, a WRONG name is a real byte charge. These rows ARE applied to target objs on every build -- obj_target_symbol_renamer.load_address_map filters only JSON-null rows and _denylist, NOT this list -- so an arbitrary pick is now a LIABILITY rather than a free choice, and refining one is POSITIVE-yield repair work (lane MAPDEF-3, db9eb318: +108 B from 9 such rows, with the `none` control unmoved at +0 B). RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (lane CF4-FIX): tools/comdat_fold_gate.py's CF4 tier -- which quoted this comment as its warrant to ADMIT an alias into the shipped build/45410914/icf_aliases.map -- has been DELETED, and all 3 aliases it ever installed were removed after retail-byte adjudication REFUTED all 3. An arbitrary NAME is a statement about OUR confidence, never about retail's bytes, so it can never license an alias (which under name_check is pure forgiveness and lifts the score by construction). Each refuted pair was in fact two adjacent addresses whose NAMES ARE SWAPPED -- i.e. a REPAIRABLE row defect in THIS list, which the alias had foreclosed. Repairing such a row is positive-yield; aliasing it destroys the evidence. Entries here had proven_identity=false and a class of 2+ VAs. Evidence: docs/plans/lane-ak-icf-bijection-2026-07-26.md.

Consumed by scripts/obj_target_symbol_renamer.py and wired in via configure.py's custom_build_steps. _denylist_unadjudicated_comment: Addresses hand-flagged as suspect but NOT yet adjudicated, and therefore NOT honoured by scripts/obj_target_symbol_renamer.py. Kept as a record of the suspicion rather than deleted. 0x82685750 (??1?$_Vector_base@VVocalNote@@...) sat in _denylist with NO recorded rationale, unlike its neighbours (0x82759310 = DrawBounds collision, 0x82553fc8 = argreg proof). Lane MAP-R MEASURED the cost of honouring it: -1 matched / -1 honest / 0 code bytes, all of it default/SongDB 118->117; honouring the other three costs EXACTLY 0 on every key. The credit at stake is mpn-ONLY -- the row is a real 40-byte function whose fuzzy is <100, so it contributes 0 bytes, i.e. it is relocation-masked and NOT byte-evidence that the name is right. Nothing here shows it is wrong either. Adjudicate on retail bytes before moving it back into _denylist.
_denylist_comment: Addresses that gen_target_map must never auto-emit (hand-flagged bad bindiff guesses / fingerprint collisions). 0x82759310 was a known DrawBounds collision (similarity 0.91). 0x82553fc8 was ?Terminate@RndMat@@SAXXZ: the argreg proof-test shows the target reads a POINTER IN r3, which a static void() signature cannot have. Evicting it is score-neutral (measured 0/0), and denylisting stops the byte-identity re-insertion that made it a permanent oscillator. 0x82b5b1d0 (system/synth_xbox/Synth.cpp) and 0x82b63ec8 (system/synth_xbox/FxSendMeterEffect.cpp) both carried ??$__destroy_aux@ULevelData@@...: one COMDAT name on two VAs, which the linked image can never do, so at most one is real. They are NOT byte-twins -- 0x82b5b1d0 is `addi r3,r3,0x78; b 0x82b69220` and 0x82b63ec8 is `addi r3,r3,0x64; b 0x82b69220` -- and both compile from the SAME base body, so a SINGLE struct-offset edit takes either one to byte-exact 100 and they can never both reach it. Both sat at 99.5% (FxSendMeterEffect's unit row at 99.31%, 18/21), i.e. one field from minting a byte-exact witness against a target whose identity is not established -- and byte-exact is the admission gate, not a metric. The relocation test that adjudicated the PropSync trio CANNOT separate these two: both target bodies branch to the same unnamed fn_82B69220. Denied rather than nulled so the hypothesis stays on the record; adjudicate on retail bytes (what owns the LevelData member at +0x78 vs +0x64) before reinstating either. Note the gate in tools/map_name_injectivity.py scores the APPLIED map, so a denied duplicate is reported informationally and does not fail -- denying is a deliberate, rationale-carrying escape hatch, not a way to hide a live collision. 0x826342f0 carried ??_GFrame@RhythmDetector@@QAAPAXI@Z and was DISPROVEN by the argument-TYPE screen (tools/type_screen.py, lane SIGCHECK-1): the retail body DEREFERENCES r4 (`lwz r10, 0(r30)` after `mr r30, r4`), which the declared `(unsigned int)` of a scalar deleting destructor cannot do -- a ??_G tests its flag with andi./clrlwi., it never loads through it. The body is in fact a destroy-range loop over two reverse_iterators (`while (*r3 != *r4) { dtor(*r3 - 0x10); *r3 -= 0x10; }`), and RhythmDetector::Frame is 0x14 bytes, so Frame cannot be the element type. THE TRUE NAME IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM BYTES: the body is reloc-normalised shape-identical to SIX of our compiled __destroy_range_aux<reverse_iterator<T*>> instantiations (and a sibling class of ELEVEN sits at 0x82b6f218), i.e. a _bijection_arbitrary-scale equivalence class. The obvious candidate -- the vector<float> instantiation -- shape-matches 0x82b6f218, NOT this VA, so moving it here would have been wrong; that check is the only reason this is a denial and not a rename. Chasing the callee's name is circular: 0x825bd3e8 is itself a ??_G whose map name is one arbitrary pick among ICF-folded destructors. Denied, not renamed, per 'an unproven map repair is worse than no repair'; the row sat at 42.76% under the false name, so eviction is score-neutral on both rulers and it stops a future lane grinding a row that can never converge. 0x826dbc68 carried ?_M_fill_insert@?$vector@MV?$StlNodeAlloc@M@stlpmtx_std@@@stlpmtx_std@@AAAXPAMIABM@Z (vector<float>::_M_fill_insert(float*, unsigned int, float const&)) and was DISPROVEN by the same argument-TYPE screen on TWO independent constraints. TYPE: the body reads f1 live-in and saves it immediately (`fmr f31, f1` at instruction 6), so a float really is passed BY VALUE -- but every declared parameter is a pointer/uint/reference, i.e. ZERO float arguments, and a `float const&` travels as a POINTER in a GPR, never in f1. ARITY: live-in is r3 and f1 ONLY, whereas _M_fill_insert needs four GPRs (this, pos, n, &x). Note arity_screen structurally CANNOT catch this one -- its test is one-sided on reading BEYOND the declared count, and this body reads FEWER GPRs than declared; the FPR constraint is what caught it, and arity_screen's evaluate() accepts an `fprs` argument that it never reads. The real body is an object method roughly `T::M(float)`: r3 is `this`, it loads a member at +0x58 and compares `lfs` against an rdata constant, then dispatches virtually through a member at +0x48 (slot +0x1c). NOT RENAMED: none of our compiled 636-byte bodies is reloc-normalised shape-identical to it, so the true name is not recoverable here. The row scored 0.0 fuzzy under the false name, so eviction is score-neutral.
_icf_arbitrary_comment: VAs whose name is an ARBITRARY pick among linker-ICF-folded twins. The bytes are true (retail folded them, so our symbol really is byte-identical there) and only one of N names can be expressed by a VA->name map, so each is worth exactly +1 whichever twin is chosen. But the specific NAME is not asserted evidence. Any tool deriving identity, callers, or unit ownership from these entries must treat them as unresolved. ***CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (lane RULER-SWEEP): 'worth exactly +1 whichever twin is chosen' was a statement about the functionRelocDiffs=none ruler and no longer holds on bytes.*** Since name_check shipped 2026-08-12 (d04c83df) a relocation's target NAME is compared, so if the map spells the folded address as twin A while our source calls twin B, the call site is CHARGED. For a GENUINELY fold-proven pair the honest remedy is an entry in scripts/symbol_aliases.json (objdiff forgives it at diff/code.rs via SymbolEquivalences) -- both names really do denote one retail body. ⚠ The remedy is licensed by the PROVEN FOLD, never by this list's own 'the name is arbitrary' doctrine: admitting an alias merely because a name is listed here lifts name_check BY CONSTRUCTION with no byte evidence. tools/comdat_fold_gate.py's CF4 tier did exactly that; it was DELETED 2026-08-13 (lane CF4-FIX) and all 3 aliases it installed were removed after retail-byte adjudication refuted all 3. Alternates: docs/plans/laneAB-icf-tie-alternates-2026-07-26.json. Landed laneAB 46f95e99.
_internal_linkage_allow_comment: A static free function is not a COMDAT and is not deduped by the linker, so the same mangled name legitimately sits at one VA per defining TU. Signature (measured, not assumed): >=2 duplicate VAs each reloc-masked match THEIR OWN unit's compiled symbol of that name AND those compiled bodies DIFFER between units -- a single COMDAT would be byte-identical everywhere. ?NodeCmp@@YAHPBX0@Z is a qsort comparator that is file-static in both DataArray.cpp (0x14c) and BandWardrobe.cpp (0x94); both score 100% and both are honest.
_name_injectivity_comment: INVARIANT: this map must be INJECTIVE on NAME. A linked image resolves every external / COMDAT symbol to exactly ONE definition, so a mangled name cannot sit at two VAs. It still SCORES at two VAs, because objdiff pairs by name inside a unit and compares bytes with (as of the 2026-08-12 flip, d04c83df) function_reloc_diffs=name_check rather than None; the invariant below is ruler-independent, but note that under name_check a wrong name is additionally charged at every call site that references it -- adjustor thunks, deleting dtors and template bodies are byte-identical modulo their relocations, so a wrong name on a byte-twin VA reads 100%. icf_class_bijection.py and tu5_map_apply_fragment.py enforce injectivity PER UNIT only; any new fragment must ALSO be checked GLOBALLY or the debt returns (it did: 738 surplus VAs before e7b8ba85, 533 again two days later from new fragments). Repair tool: scripts/harvest/dupname_rebijection.py. Identity tool: scripts/harvest/dupname_identity_resolver.py. The sole legitimate exception is internal linkage; see _internal_linkage_allow.  ENFORCED SINCE LANE J2 (2026-08-13): tools/map_name_injectivity.py, wired into ninja as `map_name_injectivity_check` beside `icf_alias_map_checked` with an `always` input, so no output mtime can make it look satisfied. CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (lane J3): `always` makes the EDGE dirty, it does not put the edge in a graph that does not reach it -- as landed, the stamp was an implicit of the `progress` edge ONLY, so `ninja build/45410914/report.json` (2,442 inputs, none of them this gate) exited 0 with a live collision, and that is the target `scripts/sync_match_percent.py --build` and `scripts/harvest/extent_sweep/eb1_measure.sh` invoke. The stamp is now also an implicit of the report edge in tools/project.py (2,444 inputs). Still NOT gated: `ninja baseline` / baseline.json, and narrowly scoped single-obj targets. Check with `ninja -t inputs build/45410914/report.json`, never by reading build.ninja (it is generated). The check is SET-based and prints the offending set (a COUNT check passes the 2eb6307a plan, which held the count at 8 while swapping which name was duplicated); it reads THIS FILE rather than the objs (?DataDir@UIPanel@@$4... was a two-VA collision inside ONE unit that no differ could see); and it scores the APPLIED map by importing the renamer's own load_address_map, so gate and loader cannot drift on which rows count. `_denylist`/null rows are therefore not findings -- they are printed as an informational line instead. There is deliberately no second, softer allow-list of known-open collisions: the remedy for a duplicate is to null the disproved rows or deny the unadjudicated ones, and both are metric-free when the surplus copy is sub-100 (measured: dMatched +0, dCode +360 B, control ruler unmoved). Verdict function is unit-tested in tools/test_map_name_injectivity.py and self-tested by `--selftest`.
_splits_fill_unresolved_comment: UNIT-ATTRIBUTION caveat, a different axis from _icf_arbitrary / _bijection_arbitrary (which cover NAME ambiguity). laneAM/laneAL filled unclaimed splits gaps by byte signature: 1419 exclusive-signature + 208 pure coin-flip fills, all anonymous fn_ symbols with no map entry, so they cannot be listed here by name. THE MATCH IS BYTE-TRUE BUT WHICH UNIT OWNS EACH FUNCTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED: only 128 of 1,531 evidenced functions (1.8%) have a signature unique to one unit tree-wide; the modal 32-byte shape occurs in 694 of 1,024 objs and median LEFT_ONLY multiplicity is 122 units. ALSO NOTE objdiff USED TO SET function_reloc_diffs=None, under which "byte-true" meant identical MODULO EVERY RELOCATION TARGET -- two funclets with the same instruction bytes but DIFFERENT CALLEES and different string/data references scored a true 100%. ***UPDATED 2026-08-13 (lane RULER-SWEEP): the shipped ruler is functionRelocDiffs=name_check since 2026-08-12 (d04c83df), so a differing CALLEE NAME is now charged where the target-side symbol carries a REAL name.*** The caveat above is weakened but NOT retired, and this is the part that matters here: these fills are anonymous fn_ symbols with no map entry, and name_check explicitly FORGIVES a placeholder-named target (fn_/lbl_/jumptable_/data_/bss_/rdata_ -- see is_placeholder_symbol_name in objdiff-core diff/code.rs), so an unnamed callee is still unverifiable and still uncharged. Byte-true here therefore still does NOT establish unit ownership or identity. Any tool deriving unit ownership, callers, or identity from these must treat them as UNRESOLVED. Full manifest: docs/plans/laneAM/fills-T1.json.
